submitted.summary: Conjecture 5.2.1 fails at k = 3 for every n >= 8 (ordinary proof; Lean certifies n = 9 for both the version-of-record and the MathDB/arXiv v3 wording); it holds for all 2 <= k <= n when n <= 7 (computation)
submitted.body:
For the restriction to cycles of length at least three, a forced-prefix argument reduces the relevant coefficient to eight permutations; five survive the restriction, giving normalized coefficient -1 for every n >= 8. This is a complete ordinary proof of the infinite family. The supplied Lean certificate proves the n = 9 counterinstance for both the journal and MathDB/arXiv formulations; it does not formalize the infinite family.

**Result and scope:** Conjecture 5.2.1 fails at k = 3 for every n >= 8 (ordinary proof; Lean certifies n = 9 for both the version-of-record and the MathDB/arXiv v3 wording); it holds for all 2 <= k <= n when n <= 7 (computation)

**Complete proof and verification sources:** [A negative coefficient for every n >= 8 in the Alexandersson-Kebede cycle-restricted signed sum: a refutation of Conjecture 5.2.1 (Australas. J. Combin. 86(3) (2023))](https://mathdb.com/abs/2611.00054) · [PDF](https://mathdb.com/pdf/2611.00054v1).

The paper page includes the supplementary proof-source JSON attachment and `extract_sources.py`, which reconstruct the archived proof and verification sources. The linked paper gives the complete rigorous argument and specifies exactly which statements are formalized.
